nodes.label: Tabula Rasa README (single source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Six overlapping planning docs were consolidated into one file on 2026-09-10 to remove ~2,400 lines of duplication; findings are filed by topic, never by date, so no changelog accumulates again.

nodes.label: M0 — the minimal QPSK model
nodes.rationale: Shrinking to one QPSK symbol, one channel h=1 and swept AWGN sigma is not simplicity for its own sake: at this size the Neyman–Pearson optimal detector is computable in closed form, so results read 'no detector can do better than X' instead of 'our CNN failed to catch it'.

nodes.label: M1 — the one sanctioned spatial extension
nodes.rationale: M1 adds N_J>=2 coordinated jammers plus an explicit inter-jammer link with delay, because RQ1 sweeps that delay; nothing beyond it is added, per the simplify mandate.

nodes.label: CGAN exploratory track (cgan/)
nodes.rationale: Opened 2026-09-14 because the findings up to 2026-09-12 (E1 impossibility = prior art, coordination question with no code) were judged too weak to carry the thesis; it tests a different idea before further commitment.

nodes.label: Neyman–Pearson optimal detector (the ceiling warden)
nodes.rationale: Textbook spectrum-sensing methodology uses the LRT to certify a detector; here the direction is inverted — it certifies an attack, upgrading 'the CNN is blind to X' into 'no detector can do better than Y', and giving adaptation cost its reference point.

nodes.label: Compare at matched detectability, not matched configuration
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable because the project already lost a headline to it: sim08-m1's '+70% channel-aware' evaporated once BER was compared at matched P(detect) instead of matched jammer config.

nodes.label: The matched-config trap (+70% retraction)
nodes.rationale: Concentrating power on high-gain subcarriers raises BER and the signature together — channel-aware is simply louder — so any gain measured at equal config is bought, not free.

nodes.label: Stealth budget = the detector's own clean false-alarm rate
nodes.rationale: A loose threshold like P(det) <= 0.5 is not operational stealth — a jammer caught in half of every frame is caught within a few frames.

nodes.label: Plot the whole BER–P(det) frontier over every budget
nodes.rationale: Reading a single value at alpha hides ordering: attacks all at BER 0 under alpha are still distinguished by where they start to hurt, so quote matched BER at 0.05/0.1/0.25/0.5 with the FAR dotted.

nodes.label: Dual-axis BER/SER vs P(detect) figure convention
nodes.rationale: The supervisor asked for one panel with two y-axes against the swept parameter, with no-attacker and omniscient references drawn in; the parametric frontier plot is the companion that supports matched-detectability comparisons.

nodes.label: Square-root law of covert communication
nodes.rationale: Only O(sqrt(n)) bits are transmissible covertly in n channel uses; a jammer is a transmitter, so 'you cannot inject meaningful per-symbol energy and stay under an optimal detector' is the SRL restated for a hostile one.

nodes.label: Symmetrizability (arbitrarily-varying channels)
nodes.rationale: If the jammer can make the channel symmetric, deterministic capacity is exactly zero — the general form of M0's constellation-symmetry result.

nodes.label: Disguised jamming (replicating the legitimate codebook)
nodes.rationale: A jammer replicating the legitimate codebook is indistinguishable at the receiver; the published defence is breaking the symmetry with shared secret randomness (SP-OFDM).

nodes.label: Bash, Goeckel & Towsley — square root law (ISIT 2012 / JSAC 2013)
nodes.author: Bash, Goeckel, Towsley

nodes.label: Csiszár & Narayan 1988 — AVC symmetrizability
nodes.author: Csiszár, Narayan

nodes.label: Li et al. (TIFS 2016/2020) — disguised jamming and SP-OFDM
nodes.author: Tongtong Li et al.

nodes.label: Amuru & Buehrer — optimal jamming strategies, impact of modulation
nodes.author: Amuru, Buehrer
nodes.rationale: The closed-form BER-maximising jammer against known QPSK is a two-level pulsed distribution; Theorem 4 also gives the coordinated multi-jammer optimum — 3 dB per doubling, but only under perfect synchronisation.

nodes.label: Zhou, Tan & Xu 2025 — CGAN jamming waveform generation (ISSET)
nodes.author: Zhou, Tan, Xu
nodes.rationale: Reproduced on QPSK only; most link and training parameters are unstated, its figures plot BERs below what its own protocol can resolve, and its 'optimal' baseline is a matched-modulation jammer, not the Amuru–Buehrer optimum.

nodes.label: Zhang & Krunz 2023 — smart jamming detection with CWT + DCNN (MILCOM)
nodes.author: Zhang, Krunz
nodes.rationale: It is an 802.11ac OFDM 4-class classifier, so on single-carrier QPSK only the Morlet-CWT representation and the DCNN architecture transfer; it must be reported as 'their architecture, retrained'.

nodes.label: Li et al. — spectrogram CNN jamming detector (IEEE Access 2022)
nodes.author: Y. Li et al.

nodes.label: Hameed, György & Gündüz — 'the best defense is a good offense' (TIFS 2021)
nodes.author: Hameed, György, Gündüz

nodes.label: Ziemann & Metzler — adaptive LPD radar waveform design with generative deep learning
nodes.author: Ziemann, Metzler

nodes.label: Stealthy false-data-injection program (cyber-physical systems)
nodes.rationale: 'max damage s.t. D(p1||p0) <= delta' with Chernoff–Stein converting divergence into a detection bound is a decade-old CPS program — G1 instantiates it rather than introducing it.

nodes.label: E1 — the M0 trade-off frontier sweep
nodes.rationale: Measured that no realizable (blind) attack achieves meaningful stealthy jamming in M0 — best excess BER 3e-4; every stealthy-and-effective point is a constellation-symmetry artifact requiring the genie.

nodes.label: RQ1 — coordination gain as a function of inter-jammer delay
nodes.rationale: 'Does coordination beat independence' is thin (sim04 already reached the perfect-clock ceiling); the decay of that gain as the inter-jammer link degrades has a floor, a ceiling and an unmeasured middle.

nodes.label: RQ2 — adaptation cost, round-based and offline
Eight-tier attacker ladder (m0/attacks.py)
nodes.rationale: Tiers are ordered by attacker knowledge so capabilities can be removed in defined steps; only symbol-aware tiers may read the transmitted symbol.

nodes.label: Baseline envelope (floor to omniscient ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Every results figure carries the same envelope so the reader always sees where a curve sits between the no-attacker floor and the impossible-to-beat ceiling.

nodes.label: Omniscient counter-signal jammer (impossible-to-beat ceiling)
nodes.rationale: It must be both motivated away and run: cancellation is an exact-inverse operation needing per-symbol knowledge plus phase lock, so it degrades ungracefully under CFO/timing error — unlike the boundary attack.

nodes.label: Boundary / minimum-energy attack
nodes.rationale: It only has to land the received point in the wrong half-plane, so it tolerates phase error far better than cancellation — which is why the boundary attack comes first and the desync axis second.

nodes.label: Constellation-permutation degeneracy (rho = sqrt(2), d = -2s)
nodes.rationale: Because the payload is iid uniform, any perturbation mapping the QPSK alphabet onto itself leaves the received law invariant, so no test has any power — invisibility costs exactly 4x the power and needs the genie.

nodes.label: One-sided energy detector blind spot to power-reducing attacks
nodes.rationale: The classical one-sided test was designed against barrage jammers that ADD power; minimum-energy attacks push symbols toward the origin so received power FALLS and the test fires less often than on clean frames. The two-sided variant closes it at the cost of power against power-adding attacks.

nodes.label: Deployed-detector-vs-optimal-warden gap
nodes.rationale: The covert-comms and CPS literatures assume an optimal adversary, so 'how far short of optimal does a deployed CNN fall, and how does that gap move with attack sparsity' appears unmeasured; the gap shrinks 0.73 -> 0.16 as the attack spreads out.

nodes.label: Adaptation cost as the supervisor's headline claim
nodes.rationale: Di Maio: 'one can always fine-tune a defender on an attacker and vice versa — the core contribution is to show that this adaptation is very expensive.'

nodes.label: Untrainability of policy-gradient RL over raw IQ
nodes.rationale: Root cause is the action parameterisation (raw, very high-dimensional IQ), not the reward formula: reward variance across the batch is ~0, the log-barrier detection penalty is near-constant per batch, and PPO normalises advantages — so no gradient exists to learn from.

nodes.label: Reward = BER − β·detections, nothing else
nodes.rationale: The supervisor's 'most agnostic reward'; every proxy term (idle, power, kurtosis penalties) from sim01–04 is deleted because proxy rewards produced the misleading sim04 result.

nodes.label: Power as a hard environment constraint, never a reward term
nodes.rationale: sim04-run007 is the proof: GAMMA = 0.02 was negligible against BER gains, so nothing constrained power and it climbed monotonically to 4.0 — an unconstrained-power result masquerading as strategy.

nodes.label: CTDE — the jammer is deaf to its own reward at execution
nodes.rationale: BER is a training-time construct available only to the centralized critic; a deployed jammer observes its own waveform, its own channel estimate and at best a delayed noisy ACK/NACK — the attacker-side mirror of 'no ground-truth labels at execution time'.

nodes.label: Simplify as much as possible (2026-08-21 mandate)
nodes.author: A. Di Maio
nodes.rationale: His reasoning: the simple simulations already do not work, so the complicated ones certainly will not — every layer the ladder added is a liability for understanding.

nodes.label: Inter-jammer communication delay and desynchronisation
nodes.author: A. Di Maio
nodes.rationale: Delay makes it hard for jammers to react to the honest symbol and symmetrically hard for the honest node to defend — a cause, which is why it becomes RQ1's x-axis rather than an optional realism check.

nodes.label: D0 — classical baselines on the 3-D waveform link
nodes.rationale: Reproduces the M0/E1 impossibility at waveform level in 3-D against a SOTA detector: every realisable attack has confirmed stealthy BER 0 at K=1–4, and uncoordinated multi-jammer buys nothing at matched detectability.

nodes.label: D2a — learned shaped-noise control tier
nodes.rationale: A stealth-trained GAN that beats fixed jammers confounds two effects — having a stealth objective, and generating raw IQ — so the fair control is a structured family trained with the same objective against the same detectors. Result: shaping buys effectiveness (15.9 dB), not stealth.

nodes.label: attacks.shaped — 48-parameter shaped-noise family
nodes.rationale: 32 log-PSD gains plus a 16-slot periodic envelope: low-dimensional parameters (within §2.8), and large enough that a 1–2-parameter family would only rediscover the grid. theta = 0 is exactly the barrage jammer.

nodes.label: Black-box score-based CMA-ES attacker training
nodes.rationale: Not RL, because a static waveform choice is not a sequential decision problem and A.5 records scalar-reward policy gradients stalling against a CNN; the attacker sees per-frame detector scores, never gradients.

nodes.label: sim08 ablations — noise, jammer power, number of jammers
nodes.rationale: Detection is set by the jammer's TOTAL power, not by how it is spread; noise moves the false-alarm rate, not the hit rate; more uncoordinated jammers at equal total power buy nothing at matched detectability.

nodes.label: The 'SOTA detector' is an out-of-band-emission detector
nodes.rationale: A control holding power and BER fixed and differing only in whether guard/DC null bins are touched gives P(det) 0.011 in-band vs 0.999 out-of-band — retroactively explaining sim06's 'broadband always caught' wall and sim07's 4-subcarrier cliff.

nodes.label: Per-image spectrogram contrast stretch hides wideband jammers
nodes.rationale: Stretching each spectrogram to its own 2–98% contrast removes absolute power, blinding the CNN to any jammer that lifts the whole band evenly; a fixed dB scale detects barrage even on a single carrier, so 'spectrograms need OFDM' was partly a normalisation artifact.

nodes.label: Complex two-sided STFT correction
nodes.rationale: The detector spectrogram was real-part-only — a bug that invalidated a headline; after the fix the out-of-band finding survived, so it was real.

nodes.label: Frozen stack (frontier/, simulation00–08)
nodes.rationale: Appendix material and the opposite of 'simplify'; further sweeps over it have negative expected value, so it is read-only provenance.

nodes.label: sim03b — NSF policy + direct gradient
nodes.rationale: The one method on the ladder that worked (kurt −1.30, BER 0.17, det ~0%): a flow is bijective (no permutation symmetry) and direct-gradient training uses reparameterised, low-variance pathwise gradients.

nodes.label: sim04 — two coordinated jammers, centralised direct gradient
nodes.rationale: Shows a coordinated solution exists and is gradient-reachable, NOT that decentralised agents find it — one optimizer ran over both agents' parameters, so coordination was handed over by the optimizer.

nodes.label: sim06 — OFDM + EfficientNet-B0 detector (99.79%)
nodes.rationale: Matching Li et al.'s published numbers exactly confirmed OFDM structure was the missing piece and gave the project a credible SOTA defender to attack.

nodes.label: sim07 — blind causal MAPPO under a black-box threat model
GMM permutation symmetry absorbs the policy gradient
nodes.rationale: Gradient steps relabel mixture components without changing the sampled marginal, so the optimizer's movement budget is spent on the symmetry; combined with non-reparameterised score-function gradients, PPO+GMM cannot make directed progress.

nodes.label: G1 — divergence-constrained optimality program
nodes.rationale: 'max BER s.t. P_det^NP <= beta' is not convex because the optimal test moves with the variable; replacing the detection constraint with D(p1||p0) <= delta makes it convex, and Pinsker converts delta into a bound on every detector, so the answer is detector-free.

nodes.label: Kurtosis detector (Q8 resolution)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the statistical detector because it is cheap, classical and already the sim02–04 detector; Gaussian noise Gaussianises the received amplitude whatever its spectrum, so a Gaussian jammer family has no way around it.

nodes.label: BER appears in no Zhou loss term
nodes.rationale: The generated jammer is effective purely by imitating the target modulation, so conditioning on stealth gets no help from the reproduced objective and is a genuine addition, not a tweak.

nodes.label: Jammer-on-the-victim's-symbol-grid synchronisation assumption
nodes.rationale: M0 and sim06–08 both place the jammer on the victim's own grid, an unstated perfect-time-synchronisation assumption; it is not innocuous — a grid-aligned jammer cannot cause any bit error below −3 dB JSR at 30 dB SNR while a time-offset one can.

nodes.label: JSR imposed by hard power projection on the transmitted waveform
nodes.rationale: Power is a hard constraint, never a loss term; per-frame equality projection is used because a '<= budget' rule would let a learner jam ~0.7% of frames at full power and hide inside the 2-sigma confirmation tolerance.

nodes.label: C2 — link calibration against Zhou Fig. 6
nodes.rationale: Fitting was considered and rejected: the paper's Noise curve fits no single sps and its far-left Optimal points show signs of not being plain simulation output, so sps 8 / RRC 0.35 / white noise are stated assumptions with the calibration kept only as a record.

nodes.label: Asynchronous random-phase structured jammer model
nodes.rationale: A jammer is not synchronised to its victim unless that is assumed; 'no offset' silently assumes the victim's clock and carrier phase are known. Applying one sync model to both structured jammers is what overturned the first-reported reproduction.

nodes.label: CGAN step 1 — partial reproduction of Zhou 2025
nodes.rationale: The headline (GAN beats white noise by 4.4–6.7 dB at BER 1e-3) reproduces; the ordering Optimal >= GAN does not — under one consistent sync model the GAN beats 'optimal', and the low-JSR curve shapes are a link property, not a GAN problem.

nodes.label: Overleaf paper subtree (read-only in this repo)
nodes.rationale: Overleaf is authoritative and syncs to a private GitHub mirror; this repo only pulls, so edits happen in Overleaf by the user and no token is ever embedded in the remote URL.

nodes.author: A. Di Maio

nodes.label: ITET/TIK compute migration (README §1.5)
CLAUDE.md — operating rules for this repo
Frozen-directory rule (sim00–08, frontier/)
nodes.rationale: The supervisor's standing mandate is 'simplify, as much as possible', so frozen appendix code is never extended or re-run; live work happens only in m0/, cgan/ and sim08_ablation/.

nodes.label: sim08_ablation/ as the one sanctioned path for new sweeps
nodes.rationale: It imports simulation08/ and simulation06/ read-only and adds its own evaluate, so new axes never touch frontier_channel.py; submit_verify.sh re-measures frozen job 102390's points as a regression check.

nodes.label: Never compute on the login node
nodes.rationale: M0 is the practical exception (pure PyTorch, CPU, seconds); cgan/ has none, because its link imports Sionna which cannot load on the login node — so even cgan/verify.py goes through sbatch.

nodes.label: verify.py — the test suite (measured vs closed-form)
nodes.rationale: There is no package and no test framework, so the suite checks measured quantities against closed-form predictions (BER vs Q(1/(sigma sqrt2)), SER vs 1-(1-BER)^2, each attack vs its geometric prediction, each detector's realised FAR vs its target).

nodes.label: build_attack → (d, x): equalised perturbation vs transmitted waveform
nodes.rationale: d is what lands on the victim's constellation (causes BER) and x is what a detector sees; the hard power budget applies to x, never to d — that separation is what makes the effectiveness/detectability trade-off measurable at all.

nodes.label: Detector contract: larger = more suspicious + calibrate(stat_clean, alpha)
nodes.rationale: Setting the threshold from the empirical (1−alpha) quantile of clean frames makes the false-alarm rate honoured by construction, so detectors stay comparable across representations.

nodes.label: Invariant P_NP >= P_learned >= P_energy
nodes.rationale: An 'optimal' detector losing to a CNN means the maths is wrong, so verify.py asserts the ordering everywhere.

nodes.label: Hard IQ histogram is not differentiable
nodes.rationale: Soft-bin or KDE it if a learned detector must sit inside a training loop; np_statistic is differentiable as written, and since the NP test depends on the attack law, a moving generator moves the optimal test — recompute the LRT rather than learn it.

nodes.label: Library split — plain-PyTorch GAN, Sionna link
nodes.rationale: Zhou's model is a custom composite of seven loss terms on 1-D I/Q, so a GAN framework would be overridden exactly where the paper is specific; step 2 changes the objective, which is easiest when every term is visible in one file.

nodes.label: artifacts/simXX output convention
nodes.rationale: Keeping every run's plots, model and hyperparameters in one place makes runs discoverable and lets a model trained in one simulation be evaluated in another; runs/ holds only SLURM logs.

nodes.label: Do not create new planning/status markdown files
nodes.rationale: A 2026-09-10 consolidation deleted six overlapping docs into README.md; additions go into the relevant README section instead.

nodes.label: r2c — ready-to-clear handoff protocol
nodes.rationale: A finding that exists only in the conversation is lost the moment context clears, so the README must be folded, corrected, deduplicated and mechanically re-validated before a wipe — with no changelog section, which is how duplication accumulated before.

nodes.label: source_papers/ — IEEE-licensed ETH copies, git-ignored
ITET / TIK cluster notes
SLURM_CONF export requirement on the submit host
nodes.source_location: The one thing that has to be set
nodes.rationale: SEPP slurm-23.11 clients ship without a slurm.conf and fall back to a DNS SRV lookup that does not resolve in ee.ethz.ch; compute nodes have their own conf, so it is submit-host-only.

nodes.label: Lua submit plugin overrides --partition
nodes.rationale: JobSubmitPlugins=lua clears any requested partition and sets it from account membership, so setting it is silently useless.

nodes.label: Pin CUDA 12.8 torch wheels
nodes.source_location: Two traps that cost real time
nodes.rationale: Default torch wheels pull nvidia-*-cu13 which needs driver >= 580, while every GPU node here runs 535.261.03; CUDA 12.x minor-version compatibility makes cu128 work, cu13 does not.

nodes.label: Pascal (TITAN Xp) exclusion constraint
nodes.source_location: Two traps that cost real time
nodes.rationale: tikgpu02/03 are sm_61 and torch 2.9.1 ships sm_70–sm_120 only, so jobs landing there die with 'no kernel image is available'; Sionna 2.0.1 requires torch >= 2.9.1, so downgrading is not an option.

nodes.label: Invisible home quota trap
nodes.rationale: df reports the whole NFS export and the RPC quota service is unreachable, so the ceiling (~8.5 G) is invisible until a build dies with 'Disk quota exceeded'; the 7.3 G venv simply does not fit and belongs on net_scratch.

nodes.label: bt_env virtual environment on net_scratch
nodes.rationale: System python has no pip and no ensurepip (Debian strips them), so uv is the only practical route to build or rebuild it.

nodes.label: SBATCH job template
nodes.rationale: --gres=gpu:1 (never --gpus=1), explicit --mem because DefMemPerCPU is only 6144, and no --partition because the plugin sets it.

nodes.label: Lifted 1-job concurrency cap (MaxJobsPU)
nodes.rationale: INFK's MaxJobsPU=1 forced every sweep to be serial and shaped every earlier experiment's design; on ITET parallel array jobs are possible and walltime rises from 1 h to 2 days.

nodes.label: import sionna fails on the login node
nodes.rationale: libLLVM.so is missing and the login CPU lacks fma, so DrJit's LLVM fallback shuts down; it works on compute nodes via the CUDA variant.

nodes.label: Submit-script migration (all 19 scripts)
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded paths were replaced with cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR", so scripts must still be submitted from each sim directory.

nodes.label: Proposal — Cooperative Multi-Agent Generative Jamming of UAV Networks under Detection Constraints
nodes.author: Rahul Rahman

nodes.label: Reactive countermeasures as a single point of failure
nodes.rationale: Every learned UAV anti-jamming response is gated on a detector output, so an attack that stays statistically indistinguishable from the un-jammed condition never invokes the countermeasure — the defense does not degrade gracefully, it simply never activates.

nodes.label: Proposal RQ1 — stealthy cooperative generative jamming vs baselines
Proposal RQ2 — countermeasure-level evaluation
Proposal RQ3 — adaptation cost as a round-based offline game
Minimal model first (methodology)
nodes.rationale: Layers are added one at a time, each justified by a question the previous layer could not answer — not for simplicity's sake, but because in a small model the defender's optimal decision rule is analytically available, which upgrades 'this trained detector fails' into 'no detector can do better'.

nodes.label: Proposal evaluation convention — matched detectability + full envelope
nodes.rationale: An attack that raises the error rate by raising its own signature is not an improvement, so strategies are compared at matched detectability rather than at equal transmit power, and every figure carries the no-attacker-to-omniscient envelope.

nodes.label: Proposal risk — the learner may not separate from the closed form
nodes.rationale: Against an independent, uniformly distributed payload the minimum-energy perturbation is available analytically and a learner can at best rediscover it; the ablation is scheduled early so a negative result redirects work to the coordinated multi-jammer setting where no closed form exists.

nodes.label: Proposal seven-phase work plan
nodes.rationale: Phases 1–3 are prerequisites; 5–7 are ordered by expected value and may be truncated from the end.
